preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner or authorized address
Contract must have trading enabled (tradingOpen = true)
Victim user must hold some tokens to be affected by fee increase

violation_target.exploit_hint: As owner/authorized, call setFees() with extremely high fee values (e.g., 9900 for each fee component and feeDenominator 10000) to set total fee to 99%. Then perform token transfers with victim users to extract excessive fees. The fees accumulate in the contract and can be withdrawn via manualSend() to marketingFeeReceiver (which owner controls).

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract allows authorized addresses (owner or authorized users) to set fees arbitrarily high via setFees(). By setting fees to 99%, any token transfer (except from fee-exempt addresses) will incur a 99% fee, which accumulates in the contract as tokens. These tokens are automatically swapped to ETH via swapBack() when conditions are met, and the ETH can be withdrawn by the marketingFeeReceiver via manualSend(). The attacker can become authorized (by impersonating owner), set fees to 99%, set themselves as marketingFeeReceiver, then trigger transfers to collect fees and withdraw ETH.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner to authorize attacker address. 2. Enable trading. 3. Set fees to 99%. 4. Set attacker as marketingFeeReceiver. 5. Get tokens from initial holder to a non-exempt address. 6. Have that address transfer tokens to trigger fee collection. 7. Withdraw accumulated ETH via manualSend().
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Read owner from storage slot 0. 2. vm.startPrank(owner) to impersonate owner. 3. Call authorize(attacker) to make attacker authorized. 4. Stop prank. 5. As attacker, call tradingStatus(true). 6. Call setFees(3300, 3300, 3300, 0, 10000) to set 99% total fee (or 9900,0,0,0,10000). 7. Call setFeeReceivers(DEAD, attacker) to set attacker as marketingFeeReceiver. 8. Impersonate initial holder (0x4CE6D95Ba0f6CBEa8CdC43E1a77359E609bC730C). 9. Transfer some tokens from initial holder to victim1 (non-exempt). 10. Have victim1 transfer tokens to victim2, incurring 99% fee. 11. Ensure swapBack() triggers (or manually trigger by calling transfer on contract). 12. Call manualSend() as attacker to withdraw ETH.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The key issue is that fees accumulate as tokens in the contract, which need to be swapped to ETH via swapBack(). swapBack() only triggers when contract token balance >= swapThreshold, which defaults to 1% of total supply (10 billion tokens). With small test transfers, this threshold is never reached, so no ETH accumulates. Need to lower swapThreshold first.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Assume attacker is already authorized (precondition). 2. Lower swapThreshold to a small value. 3. Set fees to 99%. 4. Set attacker as marketingFeeReceiver. 5. Get tokens to a non-exempt address. 6. Transfer to trigger fee collection and swap. 7. Withdraw ETH via manualSend().
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. As authorized attacker, call setSwapBackSettings(true, smallAmount) to lower threshold. 2. Call setFees() to set 99% fee. 3. Call setFeeReceivers() to set attacker as marketing receiver. 4. Impersonate initial holder to transfer tokens to victim (non-exempt). 5. Have victim transfer tokens to trigger fee and swap. 6. Call manualSend() to withdraw ETH.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC likely timed out because: 1. swapThreshold was too high, so swapBack() never triggered, leaving no ETH to withdraw. 2. Reading owner from slot 0 might be incorrect. 3. The distributor.process() might be consuming too much gas. 4. The test timed out after 120 seconds, suggesting an infinite loop or very long execution.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: To exploit, I need to become authorized. The contract has a getOwner() function that returns the owner address. I can call this, then impersonate the owner to authorize myself.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Call getOwner() to get owner address. 2. Impersonate owner to authorize attacker. 3. Lower swapThreshold. 4. Set high fees. 5. Set attacker as marketingFeeReceiver. 6. Get tokens to victim. 7. Trigger fee collection. 8. Withdraw ETH.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Call target.getOwner() to get owner address. 2. vm.startPrank(owner) and call target.authorize(attacker). 3. Stop prank. 4. As authorized attacker, proceed with rest of exploit.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because attacker is not authorized. The precondition says attacker must be owner/authorized, but the test doesn't automatically make us authorized. Need to first get the owner address, impersonate owner to authorize attacker, then proceed.
